what_its_for: Balsalazide is used to treat mild to moderate ulcerative colitis, which is a condition that causes inflammation and sores in your large intestine (colon). It helps reduce swelling, pain, and the number of bowel movements you have each day.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsules whole with a full glass of water. You can take this medicine with or without food. If you have trouble swallowing capsules, you may carefully open the capsule and sprinkle the contents onto a spoonful of applesauce, then swallow it right away without chewing. Do not crush or chew the capsules. Take this medicine at the same times each day to help you remember.
dosing: The usual adult dose is three 750 mg capsules taken three times a day (morning, afternoon, and evening) for up to 8 weeks. Your doctor may adjust your dose based on your condition and how well you respond to treatment. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and never change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store this medicine at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use medicine that is expired — check the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking antacids that contain calcium carbonate (like Tums) or magnesium and aluminum (like Maalox or Mylanta) at the same time as balsalazide, as they may affect how well the medicine works. Tell your doctor or pharmacist about all other medicines, vitamins, or supplements you take. Avoid if you are allergic to aspirin or salicylate medicines, as balsalazide is related to these. Limit or avoid alcohol, as it may worsen stomach side effects.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: severe stomach pain or cramping that gets worse; bloody or very watery diarrhea; yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice); dark-colored urine or pale stools (signs of liver problems); chest pain or shortness of breath; a skin rash, hives, or swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat (signs of an allergic reaction); fever, joint pain, or a butterfly-shaped rash on your face (possible signs of a rare condition called drug-induced lupus); unusual tiredness or weakness; or if your symptoms do not improve or get worse after starting treatment.
when_it_works: Some patients begin to notice improvement in their symptoms within a few days to a few weeks of starting treatment. However, it may take up to 8 weeks to feel the full benefit of this medicine. Do not stop taking it early even if you start feeling better, unless your doctor tells you to.
special_populations: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding before taking this medicine. Use with caution if you have kidney disease, as balsalazide may affect kidney function over time. It is not approved for use in children under 5 years old. Older adults should use this medicine with caution and be monitored regularly by their doctor. Always inform your doctor of any other health conditions you have before starting this medicine.
